title: Jr NTR's Dragon Glimpse Just Crossed 64 Million YouTube Views in 24 Hours. That's an Indian Cinema Record.
excerpt: Prashanth Neel's period action drama is set in 1967 Mumbai and Kolkata's opium trade. The KGF director calls it his 'darkest and most risky creation.' Release date: June 11, 2027.
body:
The first glimpse of *Dragon* — the collaboration between Jr NTR and KGF director Prashanth Neel that the Telugu film industry has been waiting for — dropped on May 20, coinciding with Jr NTR's birthday. Within 24 hours, it racked up more than 64 million views on YouTube, making it the most-watched glimpse ever for an Indian film.

The four-minute-plus teaser introduces all major characters, but the centerpiece is Jr NTR as Luger — a character Prashanth Neel spent three years developing. Sporting a rugged look and commanding a screen presence that social media has been calling his most menacing role to date, Jr NTR appears to be operating in a register audiences haven't seen from him before.

## Set in the Opium Trade, 1967

The film is set in Mumbai and Kolkata during 1967, built around the opium and heroin trade that persisted in those cities well after the British left. Prashanth Neel has been unusually candid about the setting.

"My childhood basically becomes my biggest emotion in my movies and in *Dragon* also it is my biggest strength," the director said. "This is more accurate than stories I've told before. This is set in Mumbai and Kolkata so cities are real — it's a story I built around the opium trade, heroin trade and that did exist during the British and after they left also. I'm just building an arena where real drama takes place. It's a very realistic attempt at the 1967 period."

That language — "more accurate," "very realistic" — is notable coming from a filmmaker whose previous work leaned heavily into stylized, larger-than-life spectacle. *KGF* was mythmaking. *Dragon*, at least in intention, appears to be something closer to period realism with commercial scale.

## The Cast and the Collaborators

The ensemble includes Anil Kapoor, Rukmini Vasanth, Biju Menon, Khushbu Sundar, Guru Somasundaram, Ashutosh Rana, and Rajeev Kanakala. It's a pan-Indian cast designed for a pan-Indian release — Telugu, Tamil, Hindi, Kannada, and Malayalam simultaneously.

The film is produced by Nandamuri Kalyan Ram under NTR Arts, Naveen Yerneni and Y. Ravi Shankar under Mythri Movie Makers, and Bhushan Kumar under T-Series. That's three of the most powerful production houses in South Indian and Hindi cinema aligned behind a single project.

## Why This Matters for NRI Audiences

For the Indian diaspora that packs IMAX screens in New Jersey, Texas, and the Bay Area for Telugu tentpoles, *Dragon* is already the most anticipated Indian film of 2027. The 64-million-view glimpse isn't just a YouTube metric — it's advance ticket demand expressed as a data point.

Jr NTR's most recent theatrical release was *Devara: Part 1* in 2024. Before that, *RRR* turned him into a global name — the kind of actor whose films get opening-weekend campaigns in US multiplexes. *Dragon* arrives as the first major collaboration between two of South Indian cinema's biggest draws: the actor who danced his way to an Oscar-adjacent spotlight and the director who turned a Kannada mining epic into a ₹1,200 crore franchise.

The release is locked for June 11, 2027. For NRIs planning their summers, that's a date worth blocking.
author: Diaspora Desk
